c.tagline: Sri Lanka's Tamil cultural capital — soaring temple gopurams, colonial forts, and island causeways.

taxi.fareNote: Metered tuk-tuks booked through PickMe are the norm in town; Uber coverage is limited, so most rides are three-wheelers hailed on the app or negotiated in cash.

emergency.note: 119 reaches the police; 110 is the fire & rescue line; 1990 is the free nationwide Suwa Seriya ambulance service.

avoid.reason: Stick to marked roads and paths in remote parts of the peninsula and islands, as a few former conflict areas were demined only in recent years.

hood_desc: The spiritual heart of Jaffna, built around the golden-gopuram Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil — one of Sri Lanka's grandest Hindu temples and the focus of the huge August festival. A calm, culturally rich residential area best for travelers who want to stay near the sights.
The commercial core around the star-shaped Dutch Fort, the rebuilt Public Library, St Mary's Cathedral, markets and the bus and train stations; the most convenient walkable base for first-timers.
A leafy, genteel residential quarter of colonial-era churches, missionary schools and old villas just south of the center; quiet and local, popular for boutique guesthouses.
A Catholic fishing neighborhood on the lagoon edge west of the center, with shore shrines, boatyards and views across the water; low-key and residential.
A spread-out northern suburb of temples, homes and palmyra gardens along the road toward the airport and Chunnakam; relaxed and local, handy for drivers.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; local supply is often brackish well water.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5:30 AM to 8:00 PM; the Northern Line has several daily trains including the overnight Yal Devi to Colombo. Tuk-tuks run day and night.
transit.note: Jaffna has no metro or tram; buses, tuk-tuks and bicycles handle local trips, while the restored Northern Line railway connects the city to Colombo and buses cross the causeways to the peninsula's islands.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the conductor; train tickets at the station counter or online. Tuk-tuks are metered via PickMe or negotiated in cash.

bus: SLTB & private intercity buses to Colombo, Kandy and across the peninsula
Buses over the causeways to Kayts and the islands
train: Northern Line trains south to Vavuniya, Anuradhapura and Colombo (Yal Devi)

transit.m: Local bus from Palaly to Jaffna town (~40 min)
Tuk-tuk / taxi to the city center (25-30 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a 10% service charge is often already added at hotels and restaurants. Rounding up or leaving ~10% for good service is appreciated.

food.name: Jaffna Crab Curry
food.desc: Lagoon mud crab simmered in a dark roasted-spice gravy built on Jaffna curry powder, coconut milk and tamarind; eaten with rice and your hands.

places.name: Cosy Restaurant
places.note: The name locals and guidebooks give first for authentic Jaffna crab and seafood.

places.name: Green Grass Hotel and Restaurant
places.note: Garden restaurant with a strong northern seafood menu; popular for group dinners.

places.name: Jetwing Jaffna
places.note: Rooftop restaurant doing a refined version of the crab curry with lagoon prawns.

food.name: Odiyal Kool
food.desc: Jaffna's great seafood broth: crab, prawn, cuttlefish and greens thickened with odiyal flour from palmyra root, eaten scalding from a wide bowl.

places.name: Cosy Restaurant
places.note: Known for kool; it is usually a Sunday or order-ahead dish, so call first.

places.name: Green Grass Hotel and Restaurant
places.note: One of the few places that puts kool on a regular menu for visitors.

places.name: Old Park Restaurant
places.note: Local seafood kitchen serving northern specialities in generous portions.

food.name: String Hoppers with Sothi
food.desc: Nests of steamed rice-flour noodles served with sothi, a thin turmeric coconut gravy, plus sambol and a fish or egg curry; the classic Jaffna breakfast.

places.name: Malayan Cafe
places.note: Open since the early 1900s, serving on banana leaves; famous for its morning string hoppers.

places.name: Hotel Rolex
places.note: Basic, packed and much loved for Jaffna rice and curry and breakfast plates.

places.name: Nallur Bhavan
places.note: Vegetarian standby near the temple; dependable hoppers and short eats.

food.name: Jaffna Rice and Curry on Banana Leaf
food.desc: A spread of rice with fiery Jaffna-spiced curries, brinjal moju, sambol and papadam, served on a banana leaf and refilled until you fold the leaf.

places.name: Malayan Cafe
places.note: Century-old vegetarian eatery, cash only and unchanged; the classic banana-leaf meal.

places.name: Mangos
places.note: Well-reviewed for its vegetarian thali with multiple curries and rice.

places.name: Nallur Bhavan
places.note: Busy South Indian style vegetarian hall; good value and quick service.

food.name: Palmyra Specialities
food.desc: Everything made from the palmyra palm: odiyal root flour, sweet panangkilangu shoots, dark palm jaggery and pani syrup used across northern cooking.

places.name: Jaffna Central Market
places.note: Stalls sell odiyal flour, palm jaggery and dried palmyra fruit; the place to buy the raw goods.

places.name: Rio Ice Cream
places.note: Jaffna institution whose palmyra and wood-apple ice creams are the easiest way to taste it.

places.name: Green Grass Hotel and Restaurant
places.note: Uses palmyra products in kool and in traditional northern desserts.

food.name: Jaffna Mutton Curry and Kottu
food.desc: Goat mutton cooked in the region's near-black roasted curry powder, then often chopped into kottu roti on a clanging griddle with egg and leeks.

places.name: Hotel Rolex
places.note: Local favourite for mutton curry and evening kottu at low prices.

places.name: Akshathai Restaurant
places.note: Popular neighbourhood restaurant with a busy kottu griddle after dark.

places.name: Green Grass Hotel and Restaurant
places.note: Sit-down version of northern mutton dishes in a garden setting.

food.name: Palmyra Toddy and Nungu
food.desc: Sap tapped from palmyra palms at dawn and drunk fresh and sweet or lightly fermented, alongside nungu, the jelly-like fruit eaten with its own juice.

places.name: Jaffna Central Market
places.note: Fresh nungu and palm sap sold in season by vendors along the market edge.

places.name: Kayts and Karainagar road stalls
places.note: Roadside toddy and nungu sellers along the causeways; best in the morning.

places.name: Green Grass Hotel and Restaurant
places.note: Serves palmyra-based drinks and desserts without the trip out of town.

food.name: Faluda
food.desc: Rose syrup, milk, basil seeds, jelly and a scoop of ice cream layered in a tall glass; northern Sri Lanka's favourite cooling sweet drink.

places.name: Rio Ice Cream
places.note: The original and much imitated; queues form outside every evening.

places.name: Mangos
places.note: Good faluda and fresh juices to finish a vegetarian thali.

places.name: Hotel Rolex
places.note: Cheap faluda and milkshakes alongside the rice and curry trade.

landmarks: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil
Jaffna's golden-arched Hindu masterpiece dedicated to Lord Murugan, erupting each August into a spectacular 25-day chariot festival.
Jaffna Fort
A vast star-shaped Dutch fortress on the lagoon, its coral-and-limestone ramparts offering sunset walks through layers of colonial and wartime history.
Jaffna Public Library
An elegant white Indo-Saracenic landmark, burned in 1981 and lovingly rebuilt, standing as the proud symbol of Tamil learning and resilience.
Keerimalai Springs and Naguleswaram Kovil
Sacred freshwater bathing tanks beside the sea, joined to one of the island's five ancient Ishwaram temples of Shiva.
Casuarina Beach
The peninsula's best swimming beach on Karainagar island, a shallow, casuarina-fringed lagoon of calm milky-blue water.
Jaffna Market and Clock Tower
The bustling commercial heart of the peninsula, piled with Jaffna mangoes, palmyrah products and dried fish beneath a Victorian clock tower.
Mantri Manai and Sangili Thoppu archway
Evocative remnants of the Jaffna kingdom's royal quarter at Nallur, linked to the last Tamil king, Sangili.
Jaffna Archaeological Museum
A quiet museum in Nallur holding centuries of Tamil, Buddhist and colonial-era finds, from ancient stone carvings and coins to Dutch and British gravestones.
Nilavarai Bottomless Well
A mysterious tidal limestone sinkhole on the peninsula whose freshwater surface rises and falls with the tide, long believed by locals to be truly bottomless.
Kadurugoda Vihara (Kandarodai Ruins)
A cluster of about twenty small ancient stupas with distinctive coral-stone domes, remnants of one of the last Buddhist monastic sites in the Jaffna peninsula.

train.note: The Northern Line links Jaffna to Colombo via Vavuniya and Anuradhapura; the overnight Yal Devi and intercity trains take roughly 6-8 hrs. The line was rebuilt after the war and through running to Jaffna and Kankesanthurai was fully restored by 2023. Sleeper berths and reserved seats sell out well ahead on weekends and holidays, so book through the Sri Lanka Railways portal at seatreservation.railway.gov.lk rather than turning up at the station. No train crosses the border - the historic Colombo-Talaimannar boat train to India has not run since the 1960s.

bus.note: SLTB and private intercity buses connect Jaffna with Colombo, Kandy and Trincomalee, while local buses cross the causeways to Kayts and the peninsula's islands. Long-distance services use the central bus stand in Jaffna town; the Colombo run on the A9 takes about 8-9 hrs and overnight departures are common. Tickets are bought at the stand or from the conductor; there are no international coach services.

intl.to: Nagapattinam (India) - sails from Kankesanthurai (KKS), ~20 km north of Jaffna
Nainativu (Nagadeepa) & Delft Island (Sri Lanka) - from the Kurikadduwan (KKD) jetty, about 1.5 hrs west of Jaffna by road
intl.op: government and private boat operators - tickets bought at the jetty

ferry.note: The Kankesanthurai-Nagapattinam fast ferry launched in late 2023 and crosses in about 3.5 hrs, with immigration and customs handled at the KKS terminal, but the service has been repeatedly paused for weather, refits and commercial reasons, so confirm directly with the operator before building a trip around it. Domestic island boats are far more dependable: small ferries run all day from the Kurikadduwan jetty to Nainativu for the Nagadeepa temples and several times daily on the hour-long crossing to Delft, for a token fare paid at the landing. These open boats do not sail in rough weather during the northeast monsoon from roughly October to January, and there is no vehicle ferry, so cars are left at the jetty.

half.name: Nainativu (Nagadeepa)
half.blurb: Sacred island reached by causeway and a short ferry, home to a Buddhist temple and a revered Hindu Amman kovil.

half.name: Kayts & Karainagar
half.blurb: Causeway-linked islands with Dutch-era Fort Hammenhiel and the shallow Casuarina Beach.

half.name: Point Pedro & Keerimalai
half.blurb: The island's northern tip and the freshwater Keerimalai springs beside the sea.

full.name: Delft Island (Neduntheevu)
full.blurb: Windswept island of wild ponies, coral-wall lanes and a giant baobab, reached by government ferry.

full.name: Elephant Pass & Kilinochchi
full.blurb: Wartime memorials and monuments on the causeway linking the peninsula to the mainland.
